verdicts.reason: Both use the same centred banner layout. Each has the same flaws: the 'AUTHOR EVENING' eyebrow sits under the body copy instead of above the headline, the logo is too small to read, the legal text is microscopic, and a dead strip is left on the left. B is slightly better because its headline is larger and the whole book sits inside the canvas; in A the book runs close to the right edge.

A moves the book to the far left, where it is jammed against the edge. The cream circle is left behind as a cropped blob in the right corner, so the circle-behind-book motif is broken and the space is unbalanced. B keeps the circle behind the book, but it still has the eyebrow below the body copy, a tiny logo and unreadable legal text.

B scatters the content: the venue line is top-left, the legal text and eyebrow float alone down the left side, and the body copy is pushed to the bottom right after the badges. Reading order and grouping fall apart. A keeps everything in one centred block; its flaws are the eyebrow below the copy, a tiny logo and microscopic legal text.

A's two-line headline is strong, but the venue line, legal text and eyebrow are scattered down the left, and the date has shrunk to tiny type crammed beside the CTA. The body copy is squeezed into a narrow column on the far right. B is a coherent single block, but it has the usual misplaced eyebrow, tiny logo and unreadable fine print.
